item.title: Architecture
item.description:
Functional requirements

  • Runs entirely client-side, including from file:// — no server, no install, no build step.
  • Loads data as plain .js files injected via <script> tags (not fetch(), which file:// blocks), writing into a shared window.DS namespace.

Key decisions

  • No bundler, no framework. Each module is a small UMD-style IIFE attaching to window.DS_APP in the browser and exporting via module.exports under Node for tests — see util.js’s el() hyperscript helper for the lowest layer.
  • A single store + reducer (store.js), split into one reducer per action-namespace domain (preset/*, group/*, table/*, …), dispatched through a small pub/sub (createStore).
  • A lazy columnar source format: each source file defines one function per field, returning that field’s values for every row positionally — V8 never materializes a field’s function body unless it’s actually called, so unused fields cost nothing to load.
  • Formulas, not eval. Computed fields use a small hand-written tokenizer/parser/evaluator (formula.js), deliberately not eval/new Function, since presets are plain JSON files people exchange.

Testing

Pure-function modules (dataset.js, entities.js, formula.js, export.js, store.js) are covered by node:test unit tests. A separate smoke test (tests/smoke/dom-smoke.js) runs the real <script> bootstrap sequence against a minimal hand-rolled DOM stub, to catch wiring mistakes the unit tests can’t see (a missing export, the wrong script order).

item.title: Contributing
item.description:
• main is always clean and releasable — no dev-only artifacts. Day-to-day work happens on develop; larger changes and bug fixes get their own branch off develop.
  • Versions are tagged on main; releases also publish a GitHub Release with the same archive attached as an asset.
  • Propose a change via an issue, implement it in a branch, and open a pull request against develop.

(This page will grow into a full contributor guide.)
